report:
Method: parsed all six samples (LinkedIn parser for *-linkedin.csv, generic for the rest), then ran classifyContact/roleStats, industryOf/countryOf/bucketsFor, seniority and buildAtlas(role|industry|country). The temp test (tests/unit/features/zzNet.classify.test.js) has been deleted. Raw output: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bivekadhikari-Documents/b8fe7f3b-1789-4754-bbb1-344a380b0722/scratchpad/classify.txt and classify2.txt. Note: vc-investor parses to 544, not the 525 the lead saw.

1. FIELDS PRESENT (share of rows filled)
- vc-investor (544), founder-operator (451), small (22), all LinkedIn: company 97/100/100%, title 100%, URL 100%, connected-on 100%. Location, email and tags 0%. Country grouping is therefore 100% "Unknown", so a country preset is useless on every LinkedIn file.
- sales-crm (328): company, title, email, location and tags 100%. No URL, no dates. Tags are pipeline states: prospect 107, customer 73, partner 69, decision maker 62, champion 57, churned 45.
- healthcare-academic (239): company, title, location 100%. No email, URL, dates or tags.
- lp-fundraising (114): company, title, location, tags 100%. Tags are fundraising stages: met 2026 23, cold 23, committed 20, passed 18, warm 15, follow up 15.
- Relationship is "direct" for 100% of every file. Nothing uses tags or connected-on as a grouping or preset, though they are the most actionable fields in the CRM and LP files.

2. ROLE GROUPS (inv / founders+execs / operators / experts / other) and LENSES (raise / source / diligence)
- vc: 21/37/31/12/0%; raise 24%, source 92%, diligence 78%
- founder-op: 16/33/49/2/0%; raise 16%, source 98%, diligence 83%
- sales-crm: 21/40/17/22/0%; raise 21%, source 71%, diligence 79%
- healthcare: 0/18/18/64/0%; raise 0%, source 34%, diligence 96%
- lp: 100/0/0/0/0%; raise 100%, source 28%, diligence 0%
- small: 32/23/41/5/0%; raise 32%, source 95%, diligence 68%
No contact in any file falls outside every lens. "Everyone else" is 0 everywhere.

Meaningless lenses:
- Source matches 71-98% of five files, and Diligence matches 68-96% of five. They filter nothing because operator, executive and professional all carry diligence and/or source.
- Raise is 0% on healthcare (a dead button) and 100% on the LP list (the same as "Whole network").
- On the LP list, Diligence is 0% and Source 28%: two of three presets are empty or wrong for a fundraising list.
- On the sales CRM, "Raise capital 69" is pure error (see 4). For a sales team the right axes are the tags they already have: customer, prospect, churned, champion, decision maker.

3. INDUSTRY
- Other/Unknown industry: vc 20 (4%), founder 1, sales 42 (13%), others 0.
- The industry list mixes sectors with job functions used as fallbacks: "Investing", "Finance & operations", "Sales & marketing", "Founders & CEOs", "Engineering & data". On sales-crm the top industries are Healthcare 115, Finance & operations 64, Other 42, Software 30, Founders & CEOs 22, Commerce 19. The retail accounts, which are the bulk of the CRM, mostly land in "Finance & operations" or "Other", and Commerce gets only 19.
- On the LP list, all 114 are one kind of person, but they are scattered over 7 "industries": Investing 45, Venture capital 25, Finance & operations 13, Fintech 12, Government & nonprofit 11, Finance & banking 4, Sales & marketing 4.
- Wrong labels: every "X Wealth Management" is Fintech. "Managing Director, Private Markets" is Sales & marketing ("markets" matches market\w*). Foundations and endowments are Government & nonprofit.
- Healthcare has only 3 industries (Healthcare 165, Education 58, Biotech 16), so industry grouping tells this user nothing new.

4. MISCLASSIFICATIONS (from 40-title samples plus every distinct title)
- sales-crm: all 69 "Investors & LPs" come from the CRM tag "partner". Tags are tested against role title regexes, and requireCompanyIf checks only the title. This turns 69 Buyers, CEOs and nurses into investors with raise+source.
- founder-operator: 69 of 73 "investors" have non-investor titles (Software Engineer, VP Engineering, Head of Sales, Product Designer, CTO) at companies named "* Capital", "* Ventures" or "* Partners". A company match alone makes anyone an investor, because the requireCompanyIf guard runs only on title hits.
- Clinician by employer only: 36 of 72 in sales-crm (CMO, IT Director, Buyer, Head of Procurement at "Bayview Health System") and 50 of 119 in healthcare (Product Manager, Head of Growth, Hospital Administrator, VP Research, Clinical Trial Manager at hospitals).
- "Cardiologist" is not in the clinician vocabulary. 5 healthcare and 11 CRM rows become "Professional" or worse.
- Other errors: "Program Manager" becomes accelerator (3, healthcare); "Policy Advisor" becomes consultant; "Program Director@Y Combinator" becomes investor (accelerator role pre-empted); "Investment Officer@Yale Investments Office" and "Director of Private Equity@CalPERS / Ontario Teachers" become investor rather than LP; "Partner" at a fund once becomes lawyer.
- Seniority looks sound. CRM: 67 top, 125 lead, 136 other.

5. TOP COMPANIES (whole network) vs "Largest company" preset
- vc: Stripe 22, Google 19, (none) 14, Goldman Sachs 12, Meta 11, McKinsey 10. The preset flies to "Google 12" (founders/Big Tech) because Stripe is split 10+11+1 and Google 12+7 across role branches. 54 companies are split.
- founder-op: Google 41, Meta 28, Amazon 24, Microsoft 19, Stripe 14. The preset gives Google 24 (operators branch); 17 Google people are elsewhere. 44 companies are split.
- sales-crm: Marlowe Dept Stores 18, Bayview Health 16, Greenfield Grocers 14, Northgate Pharmacy 12. The preset picks Bayview 13, not Marlowe 18, which is split into 8 fragments (1+1+1+2+7+2+3+1). 58 companies are split.
- healthcare: Mass General 22, Johns Hopkins 17, Mayo 14, Stanford 12. The preset (MGH 22) is right.
- lp: CalPERS 5, Yale Investments 4, Ontario Teachers 4. The preset gives "CalPERS 4". By country it gives "Driftwood Pension Fund 2", which is meaningless. The largest company is about 4% of the list.
- small: Bluebird Labs 6. The preset gives 5.
Under role grouping, atlas company nodes outnumber distinct companies: vc 321 vs 255, sales 243 vs 147, healthcare 129 vs 97.

6. VC-WRITTEN LABELS ON OTHER NETWORKS
- "Raise capital" on a sales CRM is a count of tag errors.
- On a hospital or academic network it is 0.
- On an LP list it is everyone.
- "Source deals" on an engineer-heavy LinkedIn file is 98%.
- "Diligence" on an LP list is 0.
- Group hints ("Who can fund you", "sees deals first") assume the user is a fund manager.
- The data offers better, file-specific axes: tags/stages (CRM, LP), employer clusters (all), location (CRM, healthcare, LP), and connected-on recency (LinkedIn files only).
facts: Source and Diligence lenses match 71-98% and 68-96% of five of the six networks (vc: source 499/544=92%, diligence 427=78%), so they filter almost nothing; every contact in every file carries at least one lens.
Raise capital is 0% on the healthcare network (dead button) and 100% on the LP list (identical to Whole network), while Diligence is 0% on the LP list.

On sales-crm all 69 'Investors & LPs' are wrong: the CRM tag 'partner' is tested against the investor title regex and the requireCompanyIf guard only checks the title, turning Buyers, CEOs and nurses into investors.
On founder-operator 69 of 73 'investors' are engineers, PMs, CTOs and sales heads at companies named '* Capital/Ventures/Partners': a company-name hit alone makes anyone an investor.

Largest company is computed per atlas node, so companies split across role/industry branches: vc Stripe 22 becomes 10+11+1 and the preset picks 'Google 12'; sales-crm Marlowe 18 is split into 8 fragments and the preset picks Bayview 13; 54/44/58 companies are split in vc/founder/sales.
LinkedIn exports carry no location, email or tags (0%), so country grouping is 100% 'Unknown' on three of six files, but they do carry connected-on dates (100%), which nothing uses.

CRM and LP files carry 100% filled tags that are pipeline stages (customer 73, prospect 107, churned 45, champion 57; committed 20, warm 15, passed 18, cold 23, follow up 15): the most actionable axis, and no preset or grouping uses it.

The industry list mixes sectors with job-function fallbacks ('Investing', 'Finance & operations', 'Sales & marketing', 'Founders & CEOs'); the 114 homogeneous LPs scatter over 7 'industries', and the CRM's retail accounts land mostly in 'Finance & operations' 64 and 'Other' 42 rather than Commerce 19.

Clinician is assigned by employer alone for 50 of 119 on healthcare and 36 of 72 on the CRM (Product Managers, IT Directors, CMOs at hospitals), and 'Cardiologist' is missing from the clinician vocabulary.

Other wrong labels: Wealth Management firms become Fintech, 'Managing Director, Private Markets' becomes Sales & marketing, 'Program Manager' becomes accelerator, 'Program Director@Y Combinator' becomes investor, and pension/endowment staff such as 'Director of Private Equity@CalPERS' become investor rather than LP.
